## Simple explanation

Explainable AI (XAI) is a broad area of methods and practices that help
people understand aspects of how an AI system behaves or why it produced
a result.

## Technical explanation

Explanations can be intrinsic to a model, such as a small decision tree,
or post-hoc, such as feature attribution or a surrogate model. Different
methods explain different properties—global patterns, local predictions,
or input sensitivity—and can be incomplete or misleading if their
assumptions are not met.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Understanding model behaviour can support debugging, review, governance,
and appropriate use. An explanation should match the user's question and
be evaluated for faithfulness and usefulness rather than treated as
proof that a model is correct or fair.

## How it works

An explanation method analyzes a model, its inputs, or its outputs to
produce a human-readable account, visualization, or simplified model.
Teams should identify what the explanation represents, test it on
relevant cases, and communicate its limitations.

## Practical example

A team can use feature-attribution tools to investigate whether a
classifier's predictions are strongly influenced by image backgrounds.
That investigation should be followed by controlled tests rather than
assuming the attribution alone establishes causality.

## Common misconceptions

- A plausible explanation is not necessarily a faithful account of the
  model's internal computation.
- Explainability does not guarantee fairness, safety, or correctness.
- A complex model's output explanation is not always a complete
  description of its behaviour.
